Definition: properly, to foam at the mouth, i.e. to be enraged
BiblicalUsage: Za'am as a verb means to foam with rage, to denounce, to curse. In Numbers 23:7 Balak hires Balaam to curse Jacob, and the word is the cursing itself. Psalms 7:11 states the sober truth that "God is angry with the wicked every day," while Proverbs 22:14 warns that the one "abhorred of the LORD shall fall" into the pit. Isaiah 66:14 turns the same indignation toward God's enemies while his servants rejoice.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word draws a line I cannot cross on my own terms. I hold that God is angry with the wicked every day, as Psalms 7:11 says, and that no charm or hired curse can turn his blessing into a curse, as Balak learned. My position is that za'am leaves me only two places to stand: under his anger, or under his mercy in Christ.
